summary: Transient 5xx spike from ingress handoff latency during large embedding upload followed by runtime GPU warmup reset
description: Issue summary: Around 2026-03-10 18:12 UTC we observed a short but sharp increase in 5xx responses affecting a dedicated customer ingesting a large embeddings bulk upload. Impact: ~40% of requests returned 5xx over a 14-minute window; customers saw failed bulk uploads and elevated error rates in their dashboards. Environment: prod-us-east-1, dedicated pool for ClariMetrics, using text-embedding-3-large. Observed behavior: API gateway returned 502/503/504. Upstream serving runtimes experienced GPU driver resets and OOM-like restarts immediately following a period of prolonged connection handoff latency at ingress. Expected behavior: Large embedding uploads should be accepted, queued or rate-limited gracefully and routable to warmed runtime without causing driver resets or a spike in 5xx responses.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) On dedicated tenant in prod-us-east-1, trigger a concurrent bulk embeddings upload (~1.2M tokens across 1200 requests) from a single client over HTTP/2
2) Ensure requests are split across several connection multiplexed streams to exercise keepalive reuse
3) Observe API gateway and ingress handoff metrics (accept queue, socket backlog, TCP retransmits)
4) Correlate with serving-runtime GPU logs for warmup and driver resets
logs: 2026-03-10T18:11:53Z apigw: accept_queue_depth=98 backlog=512 conn_age_ms=2400 -> 502 to client
2026-03-10T18:12:10Z ingress: TLS handshake retry count increased for tenant=clari-metrics, avg_handshake_ms=620
2026-03-10T18:12:22Z runtime-node-7: nvml: GPU page fault at 0x7f8c.., triggered reset, driver-msg=GPU has fallen off the bus
2026-03-10T18:12:25Z runtime-node-7: runtime: watchdog restart triggered after oom-like memory pressure during model kv-cache warmup
investigation_notes: Initial triage by Support: confirmed elevated 5xx from apigw logs and high accept queue on ingress gateway.
SRE found increased TLS handshake latency and connection churn from a single tenant during a large embedding import; accept_queue saturated which caused timeouts at the gateway.

Serving runtime reports show GPU pagefaults coincident with the spike. These occurred on nodes that were just receiving traffic (cold/warmup path) and performing KV-prefetch of embeddings model; pagefaults escalated to driver reset.

Hypothesis: ingress handoff latency caused traffic to pile up and produce bursts at runtime; burst forced multiple model warmups simultaneously on a small subset of GPUs leading to memory fragmentation and a rare pagefault/driver-reset path.
Checked autoscaler metrics: quick scale-up attempted but nodes joined after the worst of the backpressure; prefetch/warmup behavior amplified per-node memory pressure.
No evidence of malicious traffic. Client behaviour: single dedicated customer performing parallel bulk upload; not exceeding configured quotas but timing/concurrency pattern was unusually spiky.
mitigation: Short-term: throttled the tenant at the API gateway for the remainder of the bulk ingest to reduce open connections and allow runtime to recover.
Restarted two affected runtime nodes to clear driver/resident state and rebalanced tenant traffic away from newly reset nodes.
Applied temporary accept_queue tuning on ingress to raise backlog and reduce premature timeouts while we diagnose handshake latency.
Customer notified and offered resubmit guidance with lower concurrency; provided immediate credits for failed job runs.
resolution: Root cause was a combination of (1) ingress-level TLS handshake / handoff latency under a high-concurrency bulk upload pattern and (2) simultaneous runtime warmup/prefetching on a small subset of GPUs causing memory fragmentation and GPU pagefaults that triggered driver resets. Permanent fixes deployed 2026-03-12: adjusted keepalive and accept-queue defaults on edge proxies, added conservative tenant-level burst controls for large-embedding endpoints, and patched runtime warmup to stagger KV-prefetch across GPUs. We also added a gating check so warmup does not trigger large prefetches when a node is under socket backlog pressure. Post-deploy monitoring shows no recurrence in subsequent stress tests. Customer bulk job retried successfully on 2026-03-12.
follow_up_tasks: ENG-4567: implement staggered prefetch across threads/nodes (scheduled)
OPS-3321: add ingress TLS handshake latency alert at 95th percentile per-tenant
DOCS-210: runbook update for large-embedding uploads with recommended client concurrency settings
CS-flag: proactive outreach to other dedicated tenants to recommend soft limits and client-side backoff
